title: 第五十三章 安凌第五十二章 枪
slug: 纳玄尘第五十三章安凌
content_zh:
第五十三章安凌
铁兴围着少年转了三圈半。
他的眼睛几乎要贴在铳枪上了。那玩意儿的造型他从未见过——一根短粗的铜管嵌在木托上，尾部有精巧的击锤结构，扳机处连着一根细密的弹簧，整个构造透着一股子说不出的精致劲儿。铜管表面打磨得均匀光滑，木托上刻了几道防滑的纹路，每一个细节都透着精心。
铁兴把嘴里的草茎从左嘴角换到右嘴角叼着，伸手想去摸，指尖悬在半空中抖了抖，又缩了回来——怕给人碰坏了。
他绕着少年又走了半圈，从上到下，从前到后，恨不得钻到那铳枪的肚子里头看看。
“你这到底是什么东西？”
“铳枪。”少年把武器从肩上卸下来，随手往上抛了抛，吓得铁兴脸上的肉都跟着抖了三抖，连忙伸手想去接。少年稳稳接住，嘴角一勾，“我自个儿做的。”
“自个儿做的？”铁兴的声音拔高了整整一个调，嘴里的草茎第三次掉在了地上，“你说这是你做的？”
“不然呢？天上掉下来的？”
“不是，我不是那个意思……”铁兴蹲下身，把脑袋凑到铳枪跟前，从枪口看到枪托，从前头看到后头，恨不得把眼睛抠下来贴上去。他舔了舔嘴唇，语速快得像连珠炮一样往外蹦问题：
“这是什么原理？怎么发射的？用的什么材料？铜管是浇铸的还是锻打的？里头装的什么东西？这么细一根管子怎么打出那么大的力道来的？装填要几步？打完一发要多长时间再装？一次能装几发？”
少年被他这股热乎劲儿逗乐了，把铳枪拆成两截，露出内部的击发结构。弹簧、撞针、药池，一个个零件在他手底下拆得干净利落。
“你看，这里是撞针，这里是药池。扣下扳机的时候撞针打下去，击打这块火石，火星溅出来引燃药池里的火药，火药爆炸的推力把枪管里的铁砂推出去。”
“火药？”铁兴像听到了什么绝世秘籍的名字，整个人往前倾了半个身位，鼻尖几乎要碰到那些细小的零件上，“什么是火药？怎么配的？比例多少？”
“一硝二磺三木炭，按比例配好，细磨混匀就行。”
“硝是什么？磺又是什么？木炭我倒是知道，什么木头的炭？要磨多细？磨到什么程度才算好？”
少年被他这一连串追问给问住了，挠了挠头，正要组织语言解释，余光却扫见了一旁的苏尘。
苏尘站在原地，一动不动。
从刚才开始，他就没有说过一句话。
那些地痞已经被打跑了，巷子里恢复了安静，只剩下铁兴叽叽喳喳的问话声在回荡。可苏尘就像跟这热闹完全隔了一层看不见的屏障，整个人僵在那里，像是被什么无形的力量钉住了。

他的目光死死地盯着少年腰间那把铳枪。
铜管。木托。扳机。
那些形状、那些构造、那些设计上的每一个细节，都在告诉他一个不可能的事实——
那玩意儿不是这个世界的产物。
它不是刀，不是剑，不是任何这个世界的匠人能造出来的东西。
它是枪。
苏尘的手指在袖子里微微蜷缩了一下。
他想到了很多东西。想到了第一世在新闻里看到的各种枪械，想到了那些游戏里的武器模型，想到了那个世界的工厂、流水线、科技文明。
他想到这具身体的原主人在看到那把铳枪时的震惊——那是身为一个十七岁少年的震惊。
而他自己——一个从现代世界穿越而来的灵魂——感受到的是另一种震惊。
这个世界，不应该有枪。
除非……造它的人，和他来自同一个地方。
苏尘的呼吸不由自主地变得急促了。他的心脏在胸腔里砰砰跳动着，每一下都像是要把什么东西撞碎。
他张了张嘴，又合上了。
他不敢问。
他怕问了之后，得到的答案是否定的。
他已经在这个世界孤零零地活了五十年。五十年，他早就习惯了把所有的秘密埋在心底，习惯了在夜深人静的时候独自咀嚼那些无人能懂的回忆。
他以为自己早已习惯了这种孤独。
可就在刚才，在看到那把铳枪的那一刻，他所有的心防都出现了裂痕。
少年注意到了苏尘的异常。

他把铳枪重新组装好，往肩上一扛，朝苏尘扬了扬下巴：“你怎么了？”

Chapter 53 An Ling
Tiexing circled around the boy three and a half times.
His eyes were almost glued to the gun. He had never seen the shape of that thing before - a short and thick copper pipe embedded in a wooden stock, with a delicate hammer structure at the end, and a fine spring connected to the trigger. The whole structure exuded an indescribable exquisiteness. The surface of the copper pipe is polished evenly and smoothly, and several anti-slip lines are carved on the wooden support. Every detail is meticulous.
Tie Xing moved the grass stem in his mouth from the left corner of his mouth to the right corner of his mouth. He reached out to touch it, but his fingertips hung in the air and shook, then he retracted them - for fear of being broken.
He walked half a circle around the young man, from top to bottom, front to back, wanting to get into the belly of the gun and take a look.
"What the hell is this?"
"Gun gun." The young man took off the weapon from his shoulder and threw it up. He was so frightened that the flesh on Tie Xing's face trembled three times, and he quickly reached out to catch it. The young man caught it steadily and said with a smile, "I made it myself."
"Did you make it yourself?" Tie Xing's voice rose by a whole pitch, and the grass stem in his mouth fell to the ground for the third time, "You said you made this?"
"Otherwise? Falling from the sky?"
"No, that's not what I meant..." Tie Xing squatted down and put his head in front of the gun. From the muzzle to the butt, from the front to the back, he wanted to pluck out his eyes and stick them on. He licked his lips and spoke quickly like a barrage of questions:
"What is the principle of this? How is it fired? What materials are used? Is the copper pipe cast or forged? What is contained in it? How can such a thin pipe produce such a strong force? How many steps does it take to load? How long does it take to reload after firing a round? How many rounds can be loaded at a time?"
The young man was amused by his enthusiasm and split the gun into two parts to reveal the internal firing mechanism. The spring, firing pin, and medicine tank were all disassembled neatly under his hands.
"Look, here is the firing pin, and here is the powder tank. When the trigger is pulled, the firing pin goes down and hits the flint. Sparks splash out and ignite the gunpowder in the powder tank. The thrust of the gunpowder explosion pushes out the iron sand in the barrel."
"Gunpowder?" Tie Xing seemed to have heard the name of some peerless secret book. He leaned half forward, and the tip of his nose almost touched those small parts. "What is gunpowder? How is it mixed? What is the ratio?"
"Mononitrate, disulfonate, and charcoal, mix them in proportion, grind them finely, and mix them evenly."
"What is nitre? What is sulfur? I know about charcoal. What kind of wood is the charcoal? How fine should it be ground? To what extent is it good?"
The young man was stunned by his series of questions. He scratched his head and was about to organize a verbal explanation when he glanced at Su Chen beside him.
Su Chen stood there, motionless.
He hasn't said a word since just now.
Those gangsters have been beaten away, and the alley has returned to silence, with only Tie Xing's chirping questions echoing. But Su Chen seemed to be completely separated from the excitement by an invisible barrier. His whole body was frozen there, as if he was pinned by some invisible force.
His eyes were fixed on the gun on the young man's waist.
copper pipe. Wooden pallet. trigger.
Every detail of those shapes, structures, and designs told him an impossible fact—
That thing is not a product of this world.
It is not a knife, not a sword, not something that any craftsman of this world can make.
It's a gun.
Su Chen curled his fingers slightly in his sleeves.
He thought of many things. I thought about the various firearms I saw in the news in my first life, the weapon models in those games, and the factories, assembly lines, and technological civilization of that world.
He thought of the shock of the original owner of this body when he saw the gun - that was the shock of a seventeen-year-old boy.shock.
But what he himself - a soul who traveled from the modern world - felt was another kind of shock.
There should be no guns in this world.
Unless...the person who created it came from the same place as him.
Su Chen's breathing became rapid involuntarily. His heart was beating loudly in his chest, and every beat seemed to break something.
He opened his mouth and closed it again.
He didn't dare ask.
He was afraid that after asking, the answer he would get would be no.
He has lived alone in this world for fifty years. In the past fifty years, he has long been accustomed to burying all the secrets in his heart, accustomed to chewing on those memories that no one can understand alone in the dead of night.
He thought he was used to this kind of loneliness.
But just now, when he saw the gun, all his defenses were cracked.
The young man noticed something strange about Su Chen.
He reassembled the blunderbuss, put it on his shoulder, and raised his chin at Su Chen: "What's wrong with you?"
